title: The compiler front end: parsetree, typedtree and compiler-libs
body: The compiler is a pipeline. The *front end* turns text into a typed tree: the lexer and parser produce a `Parsetree`, which is plain syntax with no meaning attached; type checking then produces a `Typedtree` in which every name is resolved and every expression is annotated with its type. The *back end* turns that tree into lower-level forms and finally into machine code, which the next lesson examines.

You can look at each stage with a flag. `-dparsetree` prints the parsetree (`Pstr_value`, `Ppat_var`, `Pexp_apply` and so on), `-dtypedtree` prints the typedtree (`Tstr_value`, `Texp_apply`), and `-dsource` prints the program again from the parsetree, which is the quickest way to see how the parser grouped an expression or what a PPX produced. A type error is raised between those two stages, so a file with an error shows a parsetree but no typedtree.

The compiler's own libraries are available as `compiler-libs.common`. Calling `Parse.implementation (Lexing.from_string source)` gives you the parsetree of a string, which is the foundation of PPX rewriters, linters and code-analysis tools. The AST types change between compiler versions, so a tool built on them is tied to one release unless it goes through `ppxlib`, which provides a stable copy.
challenge: First fix example/hello.ml so it compiles (`x * 2.0` mixes int and float arithmetic). Then implement `Count.count_lets` in src/count.ml: parse a string with `Parse.implementation` and return how many top-level items are value bindings (`Pstr_value`).
projectInstructions: Compile with `ocamlfind ocamlc -c example/hello.ml` and read the error. Inspect your fixed file with `-dparsetree`, `-dtypedtree` and `-dsource`. Run `dune test --root .` for the library. Edit example/hello.ml and src/count.ml.
question: Why does a file with a type error show a parsetree but no typedtree?
correct: Parsing succeeds because the syntax is valid; type checking, which builds the typedtree, then fails
wrong: The typedtree is only printed for files with no comments
-dparsetree prints errors instead of the tree
reasoning: The stages run in order, so an error in type checking happens after the parsetree exists and before the typedtree can be completed.

projectChecks.name: starter: the type error is reported
solution: the parsetree dump shows value bindings
solution: the typedtree dump shows value bindings
counting the wrong item kind is caught
